name: Senegal
summary: Succession has two regimes: ordinary law and Muslim law, under the Code de la famille. Ordinary law applies by default, but Muslim law applies where the deceased chose it, and courts often apply the Muslim provisions. The surviving spouse has a reserved share. Fiducie and foundations were not sourced.
reserved_share: Muslim law: fixed shares, sons twice daughters. Ordinary law: equal shares; the surviving spouse has a reserved share varying with other heirs (secondary source; amounts not retrieved).
foreign_law_note: No source on how a foreign non-Muslim's estate is treated.
trust_note: No fiducie or private-foundation law was found; answers provisional.
open_questions: Code de la famille articles on reserved share and option of law not retrieved.
Conflict rule for foreigners not found.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
